authority.statement: This file is the sole authority for gate decisions. The semantics SPEC pins this file's sha256 in its header and must not copy any row from it. Every gate implementation must reproduce every row below in meaning.
authority.hashPin: The one-shot regression script's first step recomputes this file's sha256 and compares it with the hash pinned in the SPEC header; any mismatch fails the run.
authority.rowKeyRule: Row ids are '<transition>#<ordinal>'. The transition field takes only the four enum values dispatch-review, verdict-observed, gate-check, human-override.
authority.coverage: Covers every decision-matrix row required by plan entry T1.1, plus the neighboring edges needed to close the loop without ambiguity (D1/D2/D3 semantics, torn store, parallel dispatch isolation, root-session applicability).

globals.activation: The gate runs only inside an explicitly opted-in project scope. Outside that scope every transition is out of scope: nothing is recorded and nothing is blocked.
globals.hashFunction: sha256 over the exact current bytes of the artifact file on disk, re-read at the moment of use. Transcribed text shown to the reviewer is never hashed.
globals.pendingKey: <rootSessionId>:<toolCallId>. The store is one file per root session, so the physical pending object is keyed by toolCallId alone; the logical key always includes the root session id. Call ids are unique (verified against runtime logs: no duplicate call id ever started), so pending keys never collide.
globals.rootSessionRule: Only root-session inputs are gated. The adapter resolves whether an input belongs to the root session before any gate logic runs; non-root inputs bypass the gate entirely (gate-check#0).
globals.roundsSemantics: rounds is cumulative for the session. Every processed verdict observation moves it: a recorded pass, a recorded reject (including a channels-disagree reject) and a parse failure each add 1. Only a human override resets it to 0. When rounds reaches cap and the loop has not converged, the gate hands the decision to a human.
globals.parseFailureCounter: parseFailures is session-level and consecutive: incremented by every parse failure, reset to 0 by any successfully recorded verdict or by a human override. A second consecutive parse failure escalates to a human.
globals.storeWrite: Every store mutation rewrites the whole file atomically: write to a temp file, then rename over the target, then update updatedAt. An automated transition never rebuilds a torn store; a human override is the only writer that may rebuild it.
globals.reasonText: All reason strings in this matrix are ASCII. Changing the language of reason text requires a verified encoding round trip first; decision semantics never depend on the wording.

symbols.H1: sha256 of the artifact bytes as they were at dispatch time
symbols.H2: sha256 of the artifact bytes currently on disk, where H2 != H1
symbols.NOW: the current wall-clock moment at the transition

decisionVocabulary.deny: the guarded transition is blocked; the reason text tells the caller what to do next
decisionVocabulary.escalate: the guarded transition is blocked and the reason text hands the decision to a human (deny plus handoff wording)
decisionVocabulary.record: bookkeeping only; the underlying action (a dispatch or an observation) proceeds; nothing is blocked
decisionVocabulary.no-verdict: the observed result is not recorded as a verdict, but the counters named in storeEffect still move
decisionVocabulary.ignore: no decision is made and no verdict is bound; only the cleanup named in storeEffect may happen

gateCheckPrecedence: Inside the gate-check section, rows are evaluated in array order and the first match wins. Convergence outranks the round cap: a recorded pass verdict whose hash equals the current on-disk artifact hash allows the transition even when rounds >= cap (gate-check#9).
